newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Arb naphtha cargoes lured East.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Arb naphtha cargoes lured East.

text.p: Naphtha prices edged down with overnight crude but firm prices are attracting arbitrage cargoes, traders said.
Naphtha June swaps were last quoted at $22.10/$22.20 per barrel down from $22.50/$22.60 on Tuesday.
July swaps were still in contango at $22.15/$22.35 but traders said the market may flip back into backwardation soon.

"The market is moving back into backwardation as South Korean petrochemical plants return from turnaround while alot of their refineries are still shutdown in June and July," a trader with a major oil company said.
Regional demand was limited to India with its tender for July 87-octane leaded gasoline closing on Wednesday and Taiwan which issued a tender to buy July 16-30 arrival unleaded 95-octane reformate.
The tender which seeks 250,000-barrel cargoes to the ports of Keelung or Taichung, closes June 4 and is valid for two days.
In its last tender, CPC bought two cargoes of unleaded reformate at $25.20 per barrel, cost-and-freight Taiwan for the June 21-30 arrival cargo and $24.92 for July 1-15 delivery.
But firm prices in the East are keeping the arbitrage window from the West open at $25-$26 per tonne with two LR 1 (50,000-tonnes) Skikda vessels loading in June heard fixed.
Gasoline held steady with the market lacking firm direction.

Traders said unleaded 92-octane was heard traded at $23.75 for June 15-20 lifting while bids for 95-octane were higher than the offer with talk at $23.85/$23.70 per barrel, fob Singapore but for diffrent timings in June.
On Tuesday, the grade was traded at $23.75 for 50,000-barrel lifting June 11-15.
